quotes.text: # Set up a subscription with Cash App Pay
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: This is a Setup Intents API for when api-integration is setupintents.
This is a Subscriptions API for when api-integration is subscription.
This is a Stripe-hosted page for when api-integration is checkout.

findings: The 2026-11-07 capture at the same canonical URL is only a 15-line variant index. It names Setup Intents API, Subscriptions API, and Stripe-hosted page variants with exact query URLs (new lines 9-15); it gives no API fields, authentication flow, eligibility, success state, or runtime outcome.

The matched 2026-05-13 capture is a 241-line combined guide that includes labeled setupintents, subscription, and checkout sections at the same base URL (old lines 10-14, 93-97, 168-172). Its path details remain dated historical evidence and are not contradicted merely because the November base rendering is an index.

The existing source is routed through wiki/index.md to wiki/stripe-index.md:660 and wiki/concepts/stripe-cash-app-pay.md:70. Its three-path structure agrees with the new index labels, but only the older capture provides detailed parameters, QR/redirect authentication and testing information (old lines 34-89, 117-166, 192-241).

Recommend a bounded correction of the existing source's May-evidence parameter and payment-success claims. Retain the old raw in factual source provenance and treat the November base capture only as navigation to variant URLs. The listed query pages have not been read here and provide no behavioral evidence for this review.
substantive_changes: The captured base URL changed presentation from a combined three-variant guide to a three-link index (old lines 8-241; new lines 9-15). The index alone establishes no substantive change or removal of SetupIntent, Subscriptions API, or Checkout behavior.

The new index supplies exact variant query URLs only. Their existence is navigational; whether their content now differs from the May combined guide remains unresolved without separately pinned, approved captures.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May 2026's SetupIntent example showing confirm=true, usage=off_session, cashapp, mandate_data, and return_url, its requires_action QR or redirect step, and default_payment_method subscription creation as dated May evidence (old lines 34-89). The example does not independently establish confirm=true or usage=off_session as requirements for every SetupIntent path.

Keep May 2026's default_incomplete subscription and separate PaymentIntent confirmation example, as well as Checkout subscription-mode session and sandbox/live UX, with old-capture dating and path-specific conditions (old lines 117-166, 192-241).
Do not add the November navigation-only index to factual raw_files or replace May behavioral citations with it; if linked, identify it as an index that routes to three variants.
conflicts: Current source lines 54-55 and wiki/concepts/stripe-cash-app-pay.md lines 15-18, 52-55 imply mandate_data and return_url are required for all three paths. The May Checkout session example has neither parameter (old lines 209-227), while the direct SetupIntent and PaymentIntent confirm examples include them (old lines 43-60, 149-161). Treat sample presence/absence as path-specific example evidence, not a universal requiredness rule. The November index supplies no resolution.

Current source line 13 calls this an integration guide without a date in its prose; its frontmatter date is May 13. The November base URL now renders an index only (new lines 9-15), so a current-behavior reading of the source should be qualified as May evidence.

The May Subscriptions API confirm-step prose says set payment_method_types to cashapp (old line 151), but the adjacent confirm curl sends payment_method_data[type]=cashapp and no payment_method_types (old lines 153-161). Current source line 36 and wiki/concepts/stripe-cash-app-pay.md line 35 follow the example. Mark the intended confirm parameter unresolved by this capture; do not substitute the SetupIntent payment_method_types field (old lines 43-60) or Checkout Session payment_method_types field (old lines 216-226) into the PaymentIntent confirm request, and do not infer a corrected contract from the November index.

Current source line 37 compresses requires_action, QR or redirect authentication, and subscription activation into an unconditional arrow. The May guide separates requires_action and customer action from PaymentIntent succeeded, then states the subscription becomes active after a successful payment (old lines 164-166). State the payment-success condition explicitly; QR display or redirect alone does not establish activation.

Current source line 19 and wiki/concepts/stripe-cash-app-pay.md line 27 present confirm=true and usage=off_session as generic SetupIntent path parameters. The May capture shows those values in one SetupIntent code example (old lines 43-60) without independent prose establishing both as path-wide requirements. Label the example and do not generalize requiredness.
unresolved_questions: Current content and field requirements of the three November query variants are unknown because the approved capture provides only links, not their pages; do not infer deprecation, changed eligibility, or a new payment flow from omission.
The current index does not establish account-level Cash App Pay eligibility, authentication success, payment finality, or any completed subscription.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/cash-app-pay, the November capture establishes only three variant routes: Setup Intents API, Subscriptions API, and Stripe-hosted page (new lines 9-15). The May combined guide describes all three with separate examples (old lines 10-14, 93-97, 168-172). In its Subscriptions API flow, requires_action and QR or redirect authentication precede PaymentIntent succeeded; subscription activation follows a successful payment, not merely the redirect (old lines 164-166). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-cash-app-pay]] summarizes May behavior but needs that condition at line 37. The new index supplies no current API contract or payment outcome.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/cash-app-pay, the visible November change is a navigation index, not evidence of path removal or new runtime behavior (old lines 8-241; new lines 9-15). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-cash-app-pay]] needs a bounded May-evidence correction: its SetupIntent confirm=true and usage=off_session values are one example, not proven path-wide requirements (old lines 43-60); its activation arrow needs successful payment (old lines 164-166); and the old confirm prose names payment_method_types while adjacent curl uses payment_method_data[type], leaving the intended confirm parameter unresolved (old lines 149-161). The Checkout example omits mandate_data and return_url (old lines 209-227), so universal requiredness is unsupported. Retain May factual provenance and use the new capture only for navigation.
